information_needs.question: How does the orchestrator's output_adrs_dir parameter resolve today?
findings: recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md line 273 is a SINGLE line listing all design-composer parameters by name only. NO default value is specified for output_adrs_dir anywhere in that file. No surrounding section defines defaults.
design-composer.md line 48 defines output_adrs_dir as 'directory where any new ADRs you author land'. No default specified.

Line 187 in design-composer.md confirms the output contract: `output_adrs_dir/ADR-<NNNN>.md` — one file per new ADR.

Default resolution today is IMPLICIT and at the caller's discretion: the orchestrator does not pass an explicit value, design-composer treats it as required, and any path the caller (or the live invocation) supplies wins. Historically the implicit default has resolved to `working/feature/<slug>/adrs/` based on observed behavior at devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1 and issue-capture-mechanism-r1.
FR-3 edit must therefore both (a) define the explicit canonical default and (b) document this in design-composer.md per FR-4.

information_needs.question: Three enforcement-surface integration points for the FR-10 validator?
findings: Surface (a) — Orchestrator stage gate: recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md Step 8 (Design Composition) is the natural insertion point. It runs design-composer (which writes ADRs), then shared-document-reviewer, then Gate 4. The validator call belongs BETWEEN design-composer return and shared-document-reviewer invocation — i.e., as a pre-reviewer mechanical check. Alternative surface: as part of Step 13 (Task Decomposition) or Step 14 (Deliverable Packaging). The Step-8 location is most defensible because it catches the violation at the moment of authoring, before any other artifact is touched.

Surface (b) — Execution-pipeline hook: per ADR-0044 flatten, the parent recipe-feature-pipeline orchestrator dispatches 4 execution specialists (execute-task-code-producer, execute-task-quality-handler, execute-phase-quality-reviewer, execute-finalize-reconciler). The natural integration is at execute-phase-quality-reviewer, which already invokes `run_phase_checks.py` (line 18, 54 in execute-phase-quality-reviewer.md). `run_phase_checks.py` (line 39-44) parallel-dispatches existing check scripts (audit_workflow.py, audit_codespaces.py, audit_project.py, validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py, check_pipeline_discipline.py). Adding the FR-10 validator as one more parallel entry conforms to the established pattern with zero new hook surface introduced.

Alternative: execute-task-quality-handler.md line 62-63 invokes validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py directly. The FR-10 validator could be co-invoked here, but per-phase invocation in run_phase_checks.py is the more economical option (one repo-wide scan per phase rather than per-task).

Surface (c) — Packager check call-site: finalize-deliverable-packager.md '### 3. ADR cross-location check' at lines 56-63 (the retired BLOCKER prose) is the EXACT call-site for the replacement. FR-1 deletes that prose; FR-10 inserts a subprocess call to the validator at the same procedural location, emitting BLOCKER findings into the packager-report.json in the same shape as the existing dual-location BLOCKER did.

All three surfaces are non-redundant (per NFR-6): orchestrator surface (a) catches author-time violations PRE-review; execution-pipeline surface (b) catches runtime violations during phase execution (catches violations introduced by per-task-code-producer); packager surface (c) catches finalize-time violations as the last line of defense before Gate 6.

information_needs.question: Existing validation-script invocation patterns used by auditing-shared/scripts/?
findings: CLI shape: positional args, Python stdlib only. Examples: `python3 pedagogical_marker_check.py <skill-path> <findings.json>`, `python3 scan_memory_secrets.py <path>`.

Imports observed across the scripts directory (in order of prevalence): json, re, sys, pathlib.Path, typing, argparse, concurrent.futures, subprocess. Strictly stdlib — no third-party dependencies. Matches NFR-8 posture.

Exit-code convention: `sys.exit(0)` for clean, `sys.exit(2)` for blocker-present (the 'canonical blocker present' code recognized by run_phase_checks.py line 59). Non-canonical non-zero codes are treated as failures by the coordinator.
Output format: JSON to stdout, structured per the script's purpose. run_phase_checks.py parses each script's stdout as JSON; non-JSON stdout is surfaced as an _error finding.
Subprocess dispatch shape: run_phase_checks.py uses `subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)`. Default 120s timeout per invocation.

Canonical-home pattern (per ADR-0031): scripts live at .claude/skills/auditing-shared/scripts/; family-coordinator skills (auditing-cc-configs, auditing-github-actions, auditing-codespaces, etc.) subprocess-dispatch into the canonical scripts rather than maintaining copies.
Test fixtures: auditing-shared/scripts/test_fixtures/ exists. Self-test convention: smoke_test_auditing_shared.py exists at the scripts/ root.

Recommendation: FR-10 validator name should be `validate_adr_placement.py` (mirrors `validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py` naming), live at .claude/skills/auditing-shared/scripts/, accept zero or one positional arg (repo root, defaulting to cwd), emit JSON findings to stdout, exit 0 on clean / 2 on violations, and be added to run_phase_checks.py's parallel dispatch set.
